label: UGC NET June 2026 Paper 2 — Time Series questions not in the 1–50 set (booklet numbers not known; identified by official question ID)

items.stem: For the AR(1) process yₜ = 0.6yₜ₋₁ + εₜ, with E(εₜ) = 0, E(εₜ²) = 4, the variance of yₜ is
items.explanation: Idea: for a stationary AR(1), take variances on both sides of yₜ = φyₜ₋₁ + εₜ: Var(y) = φ²Var(y) + σ². Solve for Var(y). Option 10 comes from dividing by 1 − φ instead of 1 − φ². Working: Stationary AR(1): Var(yₜ) = σ²/(1 − φ²) = 4/(1 − 0.36) = 4/0.64 = 6.25. Official answer: C (6.25).

items.stem: Consider the model yₜ = Φ₁yₜ₋₁ + Φ₂yₜ₋₂ + εₜ − θ₁εₜ₋₁ − θ₂εₜ₋₂ for the time series {yₜ}, where {εₜ} is a purely random process and {Φ₁, Φ₂, θ₁, θ₂} are the parameters. Further, the variance of εₜ is 1 for all t. If Φ₁ = 0.4, Φ₂ = 0.3, θ₁ = 0.6, θ₂ = 0.4, then the process is
items.explanation: Idea: stationarity depends only on the AR polynomial and invertibility only on the MA polynomial. Check whether the roots lie outside the unit circle; for order 2, use the triangle conditions. Working: AR part: Φ₁ + Φ₂ = 0.7 < 1, Φ₂ − Φ₁ = −0.1 < 1, |Φ₂| < 1, so stationary. MA part: 1 − 0.6z − 0.4z² = (1 − z)(1 + 0.4z) has a root on the unit circle (θ₁ + θ₂ = 1), so not invertible. Official answer: B (Stationary but not invertible).

items.stem: Consider the model yₜ = Φ₁yₜ₋₁ + Φ₂yₜ₋₂ + εₜ − θ₁εₜ₋₁ − θ₂εₜ₋₂ for the time series {yₜ}, where {εₜ} is a purely random process and {Φ₁, Φ₂, θ₁, θ₂} are the parameters. Further, the variance of εₜ is 1 for all t. If Φ₁ = Φ₂ = 0, θ₁ = 0.7, θ₂ = 0, then the spectral density function of the process is
items.explanation: Idea: the spectrum of an MA(1) is σ² times the squared modulus of its MA polynomial at e^(−2πiω), which gives 1 + b² + 2b cos(2πω) when the model is written yₜ = εₜ + bεₜ₋₁. Working: For an MA(1), f(ω) ∝ |1 + b e^(−2πiω)|² = 1 + b² + 2b cos(2πω). The official key corresponds to b = +0.7: 1.49 + 1.4cos(2πω). Source note: Under the model exactly as printed (yₜ = εₜ − θ₁εₜ₋₁ with θ₁ = 0.7) the spectrum is 1.49 − 1.4cos(2πω), which is not among the options (option 4 is its reciprocal, an AR(1) form). The official key (1.49 + 1.4cos(2πω)) matches the plus-sign MA convention yₜ = εₜ + θ₁εₜ₋₁. The constant factor (1, or 1/2π) is also left implicit. Official answer: B ([1.49 + 1.4cos(2πω)]).

The official key (1.49 + 1.4cos(2πω)) matches the plus-sign MA convention yₜ = εₜ + θ₁εₜ₋₁. The constant factor (1, or 1/2π) is also left implicit.

items.stem: Consider the model yₜ = Φ₁yₜ₋₁ + Φ₂yₜ₋₂ + εₜ − θ₁εₜ₋₁ − θ₂εₜ₋₂ for the time series {yₜ}, where {εₜ} is a purely random process and {Φ₁, Φ₂, θ₁, θ₂} are the parameters. Further, the variance of εₜ is 1 for all t. If Φ₁ = 0.6, Φ₂ = 0, θ₁ = 0, θ₂ = 0, then the autocovariance function r(h), h = 0, 1, …, is
items.explanation: Idea: an AR(1) has variance σ²/(1 − φ²), and its autocovariance decays by a factor of φ at each lag. Option (0.6)^h/0.36 wrongly divides by φ² instead of 1 − φ²; option (0.6)^h is the autocorrelation, not the autocovariance. Working: AR(1) with φ = 0.6 and σ² = 1: γ(0) = 1/(1 − 0.36) = 1/0.64 and γ(h) = φ^h γ(0) = (0.6)^h/0.64. Official answer: C ((0.6)^h/0.64).

items.stem: Consider the model yₜ = Φ₁yₜ₋₁ + Φ₂yₜ₋₂ + εₜ − θ₁εₜ₋₁ − θ₂εₜ₋₂ for the time series {yₜ}, where {εₜ} is a purely random process and {Φ₁, Φ₂, θ₁, θ₂} are the parameters. Further, the variance of εₜ is 1 for all t. Let Φ₁ = 0.6, Φ₂ = 0.4, θ₁ = 0.5, θ₂ = 0. Then the process is a
items.explanation: Idea: factor the AR polynomial. A root at z = 1 means a unit root, so difference once (the 'I' in ARIMA); what remains of the AR part, plus the MA term, gives the orders. Working: 1 − 0.6z − 0.4z² = (1 − z)(1 + 0.4z): one unit root, so Δyₜ follows an AR(1) (coefficient −0.4) with an MA(1) term: ARIMA(1, 1, 1). Official answer: D (ARIMA(1, 1, 1) process).

items.stem: Consider the model yₜ = Φ₁yₜ₋₁ + Φ₂yₜ₋₂ + εₜ − θ₁εₜ₋₁ − θ₂εₜ₋₂ for the time series {yₜ}, where {εₜ} is a purely random process and {Φ₁, Φ₂, θ₁, θ₂} are the parameters. Further, the variance of εₜ is 1 for all t. If Φ₁ = 0.6, Φ₂ = 0.3, θ₁ = θ₂ = 0 and α(h) is the partial autocorrelation coefficient of the process of order h, then
items.explanation: Idea: the partial autocorrelation of an AR(p) process is zero beyond lag p. With θ₁ = θ₂ = 0 this is a stationary AR(2). Working: This is a stationary AR(2) (0.6 + 0.3 < 1); its PACF is non-zero at lags 1 and 2 (α(2) = Φ₂ = 0.3) and zero from lag 3 on. Official answer: C (α(h) = 0 for all h ≥ 3).
